data.narrative:
Lilac Solutions, a Series C-stage climate and energy company founded by David Snydacker, has raised $315M to date. Valuation assessment relies on a comparable universe of 3 same-sector, same-stage private peers (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy) supplemented by broader Climate & Energy comps including 1 public reference (LNZA) and 8 additional private companies.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $315M total raised as a valuation proxy, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $536M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 direct comparables produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with the peer range spanning $700M to $3.0B. These methods are equally weighted in triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $455M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median point of $768M. The wide spread—driven primarily by peer heterogeneity ($700M to $3.0B) rather than methodological disagreement—reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation within frontier energy. Key sensitivities include technology maturity assessment relative to KoBold Metals' $3.0B valuation versus Amogy's $700M, and market-stage assumptions embedded in peer comparables. Stage-progression alone suggests tighter bounds; peer median dominance of the range indicates significant valuation dispersion in the comparable set.
